correctness.rationale: The zero-error criterion is that any distinct triples differ by +/-1 mod 7 in at least one coordinate, i.e. cliques in the explicit 343-vertex distinguishability graph. Independent compiled C++ exhaustive increasing-index rooted-clique search, using a separately implemented adjacency predicate, found exactly 38,259,704 8-cliques and zero 9-cliques through 0; translation transitivity excludes every 9-code. Double-counting rooted pairs yields N3=343*38,259,704/8=1,640,384,809. Independent exhaustive two-coordinate enumeration found exactly 1715 four-cliques and no five-cliques. One-dimensional max-two independent pairs number seven; three coordinate-cut classes each have 7*1715=12005 and their pairwise/triple intersections are exactly 7^3=343, giving 35,329 decomposable and 1,640,349,480 indecomposable codes. An explicit size-eight indecomposable witness was checked pairwise and by its projections. Every nonzero translation has order seven, so cannot stabilize an eight-element set and the 4,782,463 orbit quotient is exact. All assertions are finite complete enumerations with independently inspected search logic; bounded program exhaustion is necessary for these exact finite counts, not extrapolation to larger use-counts.
